task.name: Extend mechanical reviewer-value signals to code-review selection
task.story_text:
## Observed / motivation

`reviewer_value.py` computes mechanical per-reviewer value signals — P1
uniqueness ("did this reviewer surface blocking findings no peer did?") and
latency-per-P1 — with ADR-0006 clause-2 admissibility gating, recency weighting
via #1392, and taint exclusion via #1852. It is deterministic anchor-overlap over
structured findings the coordinator already merges: no LLM, no prose scoring.

It is wired into plan-review selection only. `_select_reviewers` is called twice
in `assignment.py`: the plan-review call at :3065 passes `value_enabled`,
`value_uniqueness_threshold`, `value_min_runs`, `value_complexity`,
`value_signals_out` and `value_audit`; the code-review call at :3128 passes the
completion-rate arguments and none of the value arguments. The persisted section
is named `plan_review_value`.

Code-review reviewer selection is therefore governed by
`reviewer_completion_rate` alone, which measures whether a reviewer returned a
parseable verdict. Measured across 703 story audits in this repository:

| Reviewer | Spend | Runs | Findings | P1 | Findings/run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| openai-gpt-5.4 | $1.86 | 28 | 36 | 29 | 1.29 |
| openai-gpt-5.5 | $43.38 | 248 | 168 | 159 | 0.68 |
| claude-sonnet | $205.28 | 135 | 150 | 28 | 1.11 |
| claude-opus | $84.92 | 99 | 98 | 8 | 0.99 |
| google-gemini-3.5-flash | $50.03 | 129 | 8 | 1 | 0.06 |

The completion signal recorded for the lowest-yield reviewer in that table, taken
from story #2030's routing decision in run `675e2792fa1b`, is `attempted 90,
completed 83, weighted 0.9411, floor pass, selected true`. It is selected because
it answers reliably. Over 129 runs it produced eight findings and one blocking
finding. The signal governing code-review selection cannot distinguish a reviewer
that contributes from one that merely responds.

## Why

Code review is where the reviewer spend is concentrated and where blocking
findings are raised, so it is the phase where reviewer selection has the most
leverage — and it is the one phase with no value signal. Extending the existing
mechanism closes the gap without inventing a new one: the aggregation, gating,
recency and taint handling are already built and tested for plan review.

## Acceptance criteria

- Code-review reviewer selection consumes a per-reviewer value signal derived
  from blocking-finding uniqueness, on the same admissibility gating, recency
  weighting and taint exclusion as the plan-review signal.
- The signal is persisted per reviewer and per complexity band, in its own
  section, so plan-review and code-review value remain separately queryable.
- A reviewer below the uniqueness threshold over at least the sample floor is
  deprioritized for code review, and the routing decision records that the check
  fired or was evaluated and did not fire.
- A deprioritized reviewer has a recovery path, consistent with the
  routing-symmetry invariant (#1389); the pairing is registered in
  `ROUTING_SYMMETRY_REGISTRY` with tests exercising both directions.
- Selection falls through to existing behaviour when the signal is below its
  sample floor, so a newly enabled reviewer is not deprioritized for absence of
  history.
- Tests cover a reviewer that completes reliably while contributing no unique
  blocking findings, and a reviewer whose contribution recovers.

## Example

Given a five-model roster where one reviewer has 129 admissible runs, a
completion rate of 0.94 and one blocking finding, and a peer has 28 runs and 29
blocking findings, code-review selection seats the peer and deprioritizes the
first, recording the uniqueness figures and the sample count that justified it.
Today both are seated and only the completion rate is consulted.

Follow-up to #1443 (plan-review value signals). Companion to #1388 (reviewer
completion profiles) and #1880 (reviewer re-inclusion).

handoff.summary: Generalised the plan-review mechanical value machinery in reviewer_value.py to be phase-aware (plan_review_value / code_review_value sections, phase-parameterised fold and signal reader, pluggable anchor-text extractor) while keeping the old symbols as aliases so existing profile data resolves without migration. Built the missing producer chain for code review: review_pool.py computes per-reviewer blocking-finding uniqueness (anchor overlap over observed+evidence) at pool completion into a new state.code_reviewer_value field, model_profiles_bridge lifts it into ReviewerValueSample, and apply_run folds it into the separate code_review_value profile section under the same taint gate. Wired the consumer: the code-review _select_reviewers call now passes value_enabled/threshold/min_runs/complexity/signals_out/audit plus value_phase='code_review', gated by three new opt-in AssignmentConfig fields parsed with the same strict validation as the plan-review ones. Registered the deprioritization with its paired passive recency recovery in ROUTING_SYMMETRY_REGISTRY, exposed as a nested value_check.recovery_check audit block, rendered in forge explain, and catalogued in docs/routing-symmetry-followups.md. Added 15 tests across a seam-level routing suite and a coordinator capture suite.

story_deviations: The plan review's P1-impl note claimed ReviewFinding has no `description` field. It does — a property aliasing `observed` — so the existing function would not have raised. I added a dedicated code_review_anchor_text extractor anyway (observed + evidence), because evidence is where code-review symbol anchors actually live and dropping it would badly under-detect corroboration.

Step 2 left the config-field decision open. I committed to three parallel explicit fields (code_review_value_enabled=False, _uniqueness_threshold=0.34, _min_runs=5) parsed exactly like the assignment.reviewer_value_* fields, per the plan reviewer's P2 suggestion — there is no inheritance pattern in config to match.

Added two files beyond the plan's list that the producer chain required: coordinator/review_pool.py (capture site) and coordinator/audit.py (per_reviewer_value rows on the review block, per convention 6).
deferred_items: extract_anchors does not match leading-underscore identifiers (its regexes start with \b[a-z]), so a code-review finding anchored only on a private symbol like _select_reviewers reads as uncorroborated and counts as unique. This is pre-existing plan-review behaviour, not introduced here, but it biases code-review uniqueness upward more than plan-review because code reviews name private helpers constantly. Worth its own issue against plan_finding_classifier.

Latency for code-review samples uses the pool-wide _per_agent_dur (elapsed / pool size), the same approximation review_durations already uses, rather than true per-reviewer wall-clock. plan_flow has real per-reviewer durations; matching that would need run_agent_pool to report per-agent timings.

17 tests fail in this sandbox (test_cut_rc_isolation.py, test_sprint_lock.py, test_sprint_reexec_collision.py) with PermissionError on multiprocessing semaphores and denied git tag operations. Pre-existing and unrelated — verified the failure mode is environmental, not assertion failures.

handoff.summary: Iteration 2 advisory cleanup on top of the iteration-1 feature commit. Addressed the carried P2 on config/models.py:1162 by adding _parse_strict_bool and routing the reviewer-value enablement and sample-floor fields through strict validation instead of bare bool()/int() coercion. Applied to BOTH phases (reviewer_value_* and code_review_value_*) rather than only the cited new fields, since they are one mechanism parameterised by phase and a permissive plan-review pair beside a strict code-review pair would read as an accident. min_runs now goes through the existing _parse_positive_int (rejects bools, non-ints, and values below 1); enablement rejects any non-boolean, closing the case where a typo like 'flase' or 'no' silently switches a routing mechanism ON. Added a TestAssignmentReviewerValue class covering defaults, independent per-phase tuning, and parameterised rejection of malformed values for both phases. No behavioural change to the routing mechanism itself; the iteration-1 implementation is untouched.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Missing write/producer path. The plan-review signal is produced by a four-hop chain the plan does not touch: coordinator/plan_flow.py:1316-1345 computes per-reviewer uniqueness at pool completion and appends to state.plan_reviewer_value (CoordinatorState field at coordinator/state.py:688); coordinator/model_profiles_bridge.py:82 _extract_plan_reviewer_values turns that into PlanReviewerValueSample objects and passes them as plan_reviewer_values at :291; model_profiles.py:1075-1086 folds them via fold_plan_reviewer_value. The plan's file list is reviewer_value.py, config/types.py, config/models.py, assignment.py, tests — none of the four producer sites. With Steps 1-5 as written, the code_review_value section is never written, get_reviewer_value_signal always returns runs=0, the floor gate fails, and code-review selection behaves exactly as it does today. Acceptance criteria 1, 2 and 3 would be unimplementable at runtime and only demonstrable by hand-seeding profile fixtures.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
